title: Fishermen, boaters fight to save cuts to lakes - NewsBreak
text: ​SAN DIEGO (FOX 5/KUSI) — San Diego boaters and fishermen are pushing to save the lakes from anymore city cuts. Proposed closures to Lake Miramar and Lake Murray were saved recently, but other lakes including El Capitan, Lake Hodges and Otay Lake are still on the chopping block. “It’s a way of life, and if they take it away, it’s a gut punch,” said boater Rob Magargal. Magargal raised his son, Trevor, on the city’s lakes. “From the time I could walk or remember, I was on a bass boat,” Trevor Magaragal said. The city’s proposed budget calls for closures that would include reducing El Capitan and San Vicente to four days a week and Lake Sutherland down from three days to two days. The proposal would save the city roughly $200,000 a year. Currently, Lake Hodges, Otay Lake and Lake Barrett have Wednesday as their only week day open, but the budget proposes cutting that day and having the lakes only open on the weekends. “The line item veto was something we sat back and couldn’t understand because we are paying for the program,” Rob Magargal said. “This isn’t something free and we aren’t asking for anything free.” Rob Magargal says it costs him $33 to boat at Otay Lake and he visits about three days week. he says when you include the roughly 50 other boaters, fishermen and kayakers using the lake, it adds up. For the latest news, weather, sports, and streaming video, head to FOX 5 San Diego & KUSI News.
